Banal

buh-NAL -- two syllables, stress on the second syllable, NAL; rhymes with 'canal.' · adjective

Hear It

No recording available for this word.

What It Means

Banal is boring and unoriginal.

Reporters expecting caviar found the billionaire's lunch surprisingly banal: a cheese sandwich and an apple.

Worked Example

At the gallery's opening night, visitors drift past wall after wall of orange sunsets, bowls of fruit, and sailboats at anchor. Nobody stops. Nobody points. By eight o'clock the only crowd is at the snack table.

The paintings are banal: boring and unoriginal -- so commonplace that the eye slides right off them. Banal is broader than its unit-mate trite: a phrase can be banal, but so can a building, a meal, a routine, or an evening. Whatever it touches, banal drains of interest.

How Banal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

dull

dull: not interesting or exciting

commonplace

commonplace: ordinary; found everywhere

unoriginal

unoriginal: offering nothing new

Antonyms

extraordinary

extraordinary: far beyond the ordinary

striking

striking: attracting attention; impressive

How Strong Is It? — dull → banal → unoriginal

dull vs. banal

dull vs. banal: Dull only reports the boredom -- a dull afternoon -- while banal points at the cause: the thing is so commonplace it has nothing new to offer anyone.

unoriginal vs. banal

unoriginal vs. banal: Unoriginal is the strongest accusation of the three: a banal lobby is merely ordinary, but calling the design unoriginal says its makers copied instead of creating.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — ban

root — ban: official proclamation; compulsory feudal service (Old French ban, from Frankish bannan 'to proclaim')

suffix — -al

suffix — -al: relating to, characterized by (Latin -alis)

Put it together

Put it together: In feudal France, the lord's 'banal' mill and oven were the ones every villager was required by proclamation (ban) to use -- so 'banal' meant common to everyone. From 'shared by all' it slid to 'ordinary,' and then to 'so ordinary it bores': the history of the word is the history of how the common becomes the dull.

Use the root in a new word: banish

Use the root in a new word: banish: The old king banished the traitor, proclaiming that he could never return.

Word Choice

Banal can attach to almost anything ordinary -- banal small talk, a banal office block, a banal errand, a banal plot. That breadth is what separates it from its unit-mate trite, which is reserved for worn-out LANGUAGE and ideas. A dinner party can be banal without a single trite word being spoken.
